common.ownerCompletes: The profile owner completes this step.

envelopes.name: Envelopes
envelopes.title: Envelopes: give your money a home
envelopes.promise: Name where your money comes from and where it goes. Five minutes, no spreadsheets.

tldr.a: An envelope is a purpose for money: Paycheck, Rent, Groceries.
tldr.b: Revenue envelopes fill up. Expense envelopes empty out.
tldr.c: Start broad: 1 revenue + 3 expenses unlocks your ledger.

what.title: What's an envelope?
what.body: Each envelope is a label with a direction: money coming in or going out. Every transaction lands in one.
what.caption: Your paycheck flows into the envelopes you choose.

starter.title: A starter set that works
starter.body: Pick four to begin. You can rename them later.
starter.caption: Suggestions, grouped by direction.

broad.title: Start broad, refine later
broad.body: Detail is earned. Split an envelope only when its number surprises you.

yours.title: Make it yours
yours.body: Pick a colour to spot it at a glance on the {page}. Its direction is locked once it's used, so choose carefully.
yours.caption: A colour and a direction for each envelope.

dos.b: One “Insurance” for home, car and life
dos.c: Add detail after a month of records

avoids.b: Thirty envelopes before your first transaction
avoids.c: One envelope for both income and spending

ledgers.name: Ledgers
ledgers.title: Ledgers: set your finish line
ledgers.promise: A ledger is a commitment: where you start, when you finish, and the result you're aiming for.

tldr.a: Choose a starting balance, an opening month and a closing month.
tldr.b: At closing, break even, or better, finish ahead.
tldr.c: Keep every ledger the same length. 12 months is typical.

goal.title: Your ledger is a goal
goal.body: It records everything that comes in and goes out between two dates, on the {page}. The closing date is your finish line.
goal.caption: Start, then close. Ending above the dotted line means you got ahead.

recipe.title: Three choices to open one
recipe.caption: What the create dialog asks for.

balance.text: what you have today, as cash, or as debt if you owe.

closing.text: 12 months later is typical. Shorter works if you keep it consistent.

dos.a: Close it when the period ends
dos.b: Open the next one the same length

avoids.c: Expecting entries outside its dates to be accepted

ledgers.unlockNote: Your ledger unlocks after 1 revenue and 3 expense envelopes.

transactions.name: Transactions
transactions.title: Transactions: draw your financial portrait
transactions.promise: Every deposit and payment is a brushstroke. After 30 days, the picture tells you the truth.

tldr.a: A transaction is one real movement of money: date, envelope, amount.
tldr.b: Enter amounts as positive. The envelope decides in or out.
tldr.c: 30 days, with every envelope used once, unlocks your first budget.

flow.title: In, out, recorded
flow.body: Knowing where money comes from and where it goes is the start of deciding.
flow.caption: Money in, money out, one record.

habit.title: Make it a habit
habit.body: Record the same day: receipts fade fast. Choose a moment: after dinner, on the bus.
habit.caption: The clock starts with your first entry. Back-dated receipts are welcome, but they don't shorten it.

dos.a: Record income too, not only spending
dos.b: Give every envelope at least one transaction
dos.c: Fix a mistake by deleting and re-entering it

avoids.b: Waiting until the end of the month

challenge.first: Record your first transaction and start the clock.
challenge.progress: Day {day} of 30. {n} envelope still waiting for a transaction. | Day {day} of 30. {n} envelopes still waiting for a transaction.
challenge.allCovered: Day {day} of 30. Every envelope has a transaction.

budgets.name: Budgets
budgets.title: Budgets: plan the month you want
budgets.promise: Your transactions show what happened. Your budget decides what happens next.

tldr.a: A budget is a monthly goal for each envelope.
tldr.b: Your first draft is pre-filled from your last 30 days: a starting point, not a verdict.
tldr.c: Adjust it, publish it for this month, revise when life changes.

plan.title: From portrait to plan
plan.body: Look at what happened, then choose one thing to change.
plan.caption: Example: plan versus spending.

draft.title: Your first draft, explained
draft.body: Create it on the {page} once it unlocks.

points.a: Each envelope used in the last 30 days gets its net total
points.b: Amounts are rounded to whole units
points.c: Review every line before you publish

unlock.title: When does it unlock?
unlock.body: After 30 days of history and a transaction in every envelope.

dos.a: Change one envelope at a time
dos.b: Plan savings first, like a bill
dos.c: Create a revision when plans change

avoids.b: Treating a surprise bill as failure

challenge.ready: Your first budget is unlocked. Make it yours.
challenge.notStarted: Unlocks 30 days after your first transaction.
challenge.waitingEnvelopes: Give every envelope a transaction to unlock it.
